summary: Root cause identified with high confidence (0.82, capped at 0.88 by the Critic): the pricing-engine config/flag change cfg-3120 at 12:04:16Z ramped flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5 to 100, enabling the compute-heavy GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo path (paths=20000, 2964-8942ms per calculation) for all traffic, pinning pricing-engine CPU at ~99% and saturating p99 latency at ~2.5s, which broke the internal 2000ms compute budget and caused order-service's 2500ms quote calls to time out. The chain is tight and complete: CPU (38-42%) and p99 (57-62ms) are flat baseline through the 12:04Z bucket and step simultaneously in the 12:05 bucket, one bucket after the flag apply (F25-F30), with pricing-engine-local GreeksV2 log signatures confirming the mechanism (F11, F28). Alternatives H2 (market-data-service protobuf deploy), H4 (traffic surge) and H5 (config change elsewhere) are contradicted by flat metrics across the fleet, and H3 (redis-cache saturation) is refuted by flat redis counters and no error logs. Remaining gaps (per-pod CPU split, sub-minute resolution, ledger-db and blast-radius queries) are non-blocking and cannot change the ranking.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Greeks v2 flag ramp to 100% overloaded pricing-engine CPU
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The pricing-engine config/flag change cfg-3120 at 12:04:16Z ramped flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5 to 100, enabling the computationally expensive GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo path (paths=20000, 2964-8942ms each) for all traffic. At 1-minute resolution pricing-engine CPU and latency are flat baseline through the 12:04 bucket (CPU 38.22-40.18%, p99 56.82-60.53ms) and then step to ~98.65% CPU and ~2534.9ms p99 in the 12:05 bucket, exactly one bucket after the flag apply. This pinned CPU, saturated latency, blew the internal 2000ms compute budget, and caused order-service's 2500ms quote calls to time out. Origin is the config change at pricing-engine.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-3120 changes flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct 5->100 at 12:04:16Z ('config change cfg-3120 applied: flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct=100')
GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo (paths=20000, each call 2964-8942ms) becomes the hot path for all traffic; first WARN at 12:05:21Z
pricing-engine CPU steps from flat ~38-40% (through 12:04) to ~98.6-99.4% in the 12:05 bucket and stays pinned
pricing-engine p99 latency steps from flat ~57-61ms (through 12:04) to ~2534.9ms in the same 12:05 bucket; CPU and latency step in the SAME bucket
pricing-engine exceeds its 2000ms compute budget, logging 'request deadline exceeded computing quote (2000ms budget) calculator=GreeksV2'
order-service's 2500ms client calls to pricing-engine time out, producing 225 identical 'pricing-engine quote call timed out after 2500ms' errors and error_rate jump to ~8%

Every market-data-service signal (server-side p99 ~39-40ms, request_rate ~940 req/s, cpu ~45%, error_rate ~0.2%) is flat across the deploy and onset, and pricing-engine shows no downstream-call signature; the release is excluded as the origin.

The serialization change increased latency or bloat in market-data-service responses

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared downstream dependency (redis-cache / datastore) saturated, slowing pricing-engine
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A shared downstream dependency of pricing-engine (redis-cache, reached via F4) became resource-saturated around onset, slowing pricing-engine p99 and cascading to order-service timeouts. This was previously untested due to budget exhaustion. It is now directly tested and refuted: every redis-cache signal (cpu_pct, hit_ratio_pct, memory_pct, connected_clients, evictions_per_min) is flat across 11:30-13:59Z with no change coinciding with onset, and redis-cache emits no relevant error/warn logs.

order-service quote calls hit the 2500ms timeout

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: redis-cache cpu_pct flat (F31), hit_ratio flat 95-98% with no miss storm (F32), memory_pct flat (F33), connected_clients and evictions flat (F34), no error/warn logs during the window (F35). A saturated shared cache would move these counters; none move. Additionally pricing-engine CPU is flat through 12:04 and steps to 98.65% only in the 12:05 bucket, immediately after the 12:04:16Z flag apply, with a pricing-engine-local GreeksV2 signature (F28) rather than a cache-lookup pattern.

findings.statement: Achieved granularity for pricing-engine is genuine 1-minute buckets: both queries returned bucket_seconds=60 with missing_points=0, partial=false, warnings=[] and no truncation, so sub-bucket (per-minute) onset resolution IS possible and the 12:04→12:05 boundary is resolved to one minute. No timestamp-skew or bucket-alignment artifact is evident — the flagged change log (12:04:16Z) and the metric step (12:05 bucket) are consistent with a bucket-ending-vs-bucket-starting convention rather than skew.

Because a 60s bucket average would already smear any intra-bucket onset, note the 12:05 bucket is fully saturated (CPU avg=max=98.65, p99 avg=max=2534.9) — the step is a full-bucket jump with no partial ramp visible at 1-minute resolution, so the true onset is bounded to 12:04:00-12:05:00Z (after the 12:04:16Z flag apply), one bucket after the pre-12:05 flat line.

redis-cache cpu_pct is completely flat across the entire 11:30-13:59Z window, with no elevation at the 12:00-12:06Z onset: 11:58 bucket avg 22.7/max 22.87, 12:02 avg 21.98/max 22.57, 12:06 avg 22.41/max 23.09; summary min 19.53 / max 24.13 / mean 21.94 % over 150 points, missing_points 0. No saturation of redis-cache CPU coincides with pricing-engine's 12:02-12:06 CPU pin at ~98.6-99.4% (F10).

redis-cache hit_ratio_pct is flat and healthy (95-98%) with no dip at onset: 11:58 avg 95.93, 12:02 avg 96.36, 12:06 avg 96.73; summary min 93.83 / max 98.46 / mean 96.02 %. A shared-cache saturation or cold-cache/miss storm (H3) would drive hit ratio down and/or misses up; neither occurs.

redis-cache memory_pct is flat ~69-72% with no growth step at onset: 11:58 avg 70.83, 12:02 avg 70.2, 12:06 avg 69.66; summary min 63.12 / max 79.59 / mean 70.12 % over 150 points, missing_points 0. No memory pressure/eviction pressure developed when pricing-engine degraded.

redis-cache connected_clients is flat ~296-325, no connection pile-up at onset: 11:58 avg 314.43/max 335.37, 12:02 avg 316.34/max 335.28, 12:06 avg 309.61/max 322.35; summary min 282.36 / max 348.57 / mean 311.36 clients. Also evictions_per_min stayed flat ~3/min (12:02 avg 3.11, 12:06 avg 3.27; summary min 0.78 / max 5.04). No client exhaustion or eviction storm at the 12:02-12:06 onset.

redis-cache emits no error or warning logs during the incident: only 1 WARN in 11:30-13:59Z, 'deprecated TLS cipher offered by client 46e36f97' at 13:28:54Z (unrelated to onset). No timeout, eviction, OOM, or slow-command messages. This is consistent with the flat metrics: redis-cache shows no functional or resource distress.

findings.statement: All five metrics exposed by redis-cache (cpu_pct, latency replaced by hit_ratio, memory_pct, connected_clients, evictions_per_min) are flat across 11:30-13:59Z with no change coinciding with pricing-engine's 12:02-12:06 saturation. redis-cache exposes no latency_p99_ms and no generic 'connections' metric (available_metrics: connected_clients, cpu_pct, evictions_per_min, hit_ratio_pct, memory_pct), so cache-side latency itself could not be measured directly; the four measurable signals that a saturated shared cache would move (CPU, hit ratio, memory, clients/evictions) all remain at baseline.
